podcast.title: 1999 Album Chart Success
podcast.body: Celine Dion achieved a number one position on the album charts in 1999, showcasing her continued mainstream appeal across different music genres. "A scan of the album charts also shows number one placing spite NAS, DMX, the notorious B.I.G. Selene Dion."

podcast.title: Pioneering Modern Las Vegas Residency (2003)
podcast.body: Celine Dion was one of the first artists to accept a modern Las Vegas residency deal, beginning in 2003. Over the next four years, she significantly redefined the Vegas entertainment scene, attracting audiences not just for gambling but specifically to see her performances. Her success led to a second residency at Caesar's Palace from 2011 to 2019. "Celine Dion was one of the first to accept such a modern deal. This was in 2003."

podcast.title: Affected by Sony BMG Rootkit (2005)
podcast.body: Albums by Celine Dion were among those shipped with the Sony BMG Rootkit malware (XCP and MediaMax) installed. This software was surreptitiously placed on users' computers when they attempted to rip CDs, compromising system security without their consent. "The XCP malware came on albums ranging from Neil Diamond to Frank Sinatra to Celine Dion to Cindy Lopper."

podcast.title: Performance with Elvis Presley Hologram (2007)
podcast.body: In 2007, Celine Dion performed alongside a virtual Elvis Presley on *American Idol*. This collaboration utilized archival footage combined with advanced editing and projection techniques, representing a significant advancement in the burgeoning technology of simulated live performances. "In 2007, a very dead Elvis Presley appeared on American Idol to do it with Celine Dion."

podcast.title: Elevating Canadian Production (1980s)
podcast.body: Celine Dion was cited by Gino Vannelli as an artist who, in the 1980s, helped elevate the production quality of Canadian records to a "world-class" standard, enabling artists to build careers from Canada without needing to relocate to the US. "he cited Celine Dion and Brian Adams as artists that elevated the production of records. And when he said that they became world class, what he meant was that you didn't have to go to the United States to have your career. You could orchestrate your career from Canada."

podcast.title: First Non-American/British Artist in Top Sellers
podcast.body: Celine Dion is notable for being the first non-American or non-British artist to appear on the list of historically top-selling artists. Her sales are estimated to be around 100 million copies, a significant achievement given the dominance of artists from the US and UK in these rankings.

podcast.title: Gender-Neutral Clothing Controversy
podcast.body: When Celine Dion launched a line of gender-neutral children's clothing, she faced criticism from two fronts. Conspiracy theorists spread stories linking the clothing designs to the Illuminati, while an exorcist claimed she was in league with Satan because gender-neutral attributes were against God's will. "Second, an exorcist opined that she was in league with Satan because anything involving gendered neutral attributes was against the will of God."

xref.title: Albert Hammond Jr.'s Background and Role
xref.body: Albert Hammond Jr. is the son of Albert Hammond Sr., a successful songwriter who wrote songs for artists like Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters, and had a writing credit on Radiohead's "Creep." In the early days of The Strokes, Albert was the band's business guy, booking gigs and pitching record companies under the pseudonym "Paul Spencer" (from his fake ID). He collected rejection letters by posting them on a wall. Crucially, he had a credit card funded by his father, which paid for essential band expenses like guitar strings, cables, drumsticks, and rehearsal PA. "Albert was the business guy of the band in the early days. He was the guy who booked gigs and pitch record companies, usually under the pseudonym Paul Spencer, which was the name he used on his old fake ID."

xref.title: Las Vegas Residency Trend
xref.body: Bruno Mars joined the growing number of pop stars who established Las Vegas residencies, a trend initiated by artists like Celine Dion and Britney Spears. These residencies allowed popular artists to perform to dedicated fan bases in a fixed location, contributing to Las Vegas's evolution as a diverse entertainment destination. "That led to Lady Gaga, Prince, the Backstreet Boys, Mariah Carey, Cher, Shania Twain, Bruno Mars, Adele, and dozens and dozens more."

xref.title: Prolific Songwriter
xref.body: Albert Hammond Sr. is a successful songwriter who wrote numerous songs for a wide array of prominent artists. His credits include songs for Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters. He also received a writing credit on Radiohead's song "Creep" due to its melodic resemblance to "The Air That I Breathe," a song he wrote for The Hollies in the 1970s, as determined by a court case. "He wrote this song. Dad also wrote songs for Celine Dion, where we at the Franklin Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, the Carpenter, and a ton of others."

xref.title: Successful Songwriting Career
xref.body: After his success with Semisonic, Dan Wilson has had a highly lucrative career as a songwriter, earning "real money." He penned at least six songs for The Dixie Chicks (including a Grammy winner for Song of the Year), three songs for Adele's *21* album (including "Someone Like You"), and co-written with numerous other major artists such as Taylor Swift, Tom Morello, Celine Dion, John Legend, and Pink. "But it is as a songwriter where Dan has made the real money."
